title: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU)
summary: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU) is a university in Wooster. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with OSU.

sections.heading: What OSU is known for
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU) is a public institution known for its specialized programs and commitment to practical education. With an undergraduate enrollment of 464 students, OSU offers focused academic opportunities tailored to its student body. While the university does not have a significant share of programs in health fields, it does provide some offerings in business, accounting for approximately 0.69% of its program share. OSU emphasizes hands-on learning experiences, preparing students for careers in agriculture and related technical fields.

sections.heading: Key strengths
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU) is a public institution distinguished by its dedication to practical and technical education. Although it does not offer programs in health fields, approximately 7.59% of its academic programs are focused on education. This emphasis reflects OSU's commitment to preparing students for careers in educational sectors alongside its core agricultural and technical disciplines. The institute's public ownership supports its mission to provide accessible and specialized training tailored to student and industry needs.

OSU's curriculum is designed to support its mission of providing specialized, practical education primarily in agricultural and technical disciplines.

sections.heading: How to read OSU tuition
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU) tuition varies depending on residency status. For in-state students, the tuition is $9,584, while out-of-state students pay $36,362. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition along with other expenses such as fees, housing, and supplies, amounts to $24,595. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and their families plan financially for their education at OSU.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU) offers financial aid to help students manage the cost of attendance. Approximately 27.06% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies for students with financial need. For those who complete their programs, the median debt is $19,976, reflecting the typical amount borrowed to finance their education. Prospective students can use the net price calculator available at ati.osu.edu to estimate their individual costs and aid eligibility. Additional financial information is accessible through the College Scorecard at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?204662.

sections.heading: Colleges and schools
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU ATI) does not have separate colleges or schools within its structure. The institute focuses on providing specialized agricultural education and technical training as part of the broader Ohio State University system. OSU ATI offers programs designed to prepare students for careers in agriculture and related industries, emphasizing practical skills and applied knowledge.

sections.heading: Academic features
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU ATI) maintains a student-faculty ratio of 15, facilitating personalized instruction and support. The institute emphasizes hands-on learning experiences within its agricultural and technical programs. As part of Ohio State University (OSU), OSU ATI integrates practical training with academic coursework to prepare students for careers in agriculture and related fields.

sections.heading: Degree levels
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU) primarily offers associate degree programs focused on agriculture and technical fields. As a specialized institution within the Ohio State University (OSU) system, it emphasizes practical and applied education tailored to prepare students for immediate entry into the workforce. OSU ATI does not offer bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree programs, concentrating instead on two-year degrees that provide foundational knowledge and hands-on skills in its areas of expertise.

sections.heading: Housing and dining
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU) provides housing options for students both on and off campus. The average cost for room and board on campus is $12,358, while living off campus typically costs around $10,232. These figures reflect the expenses students may expect when budgeting for their housing and dining needs during their studies at OSU.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU) graduates experience varied career outcomes, with median earnings of $51,438 six years after enrollment. Over a longer period, median earnings increase to $60,409 ten years after enrollment, indicating potential growth in income as alumni advance in their careers. For students who complete their programs, the median debt incurred is $19,976, reflecting the typical financial investment required to obtain their education at OSU. These figures provide insight into the economic prospects and financial commitments associated with completing a program at Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute.

sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute (OSU) has a student body composed of approximately 42.24% men and 57.76% women, reflecting a higher proportion of female students. The racial and ethnic composition is predominantly White, accounting for about 90.3% of the population. Other represented groups include Black students at 2.16%, Hispanic students at 2.37%, and Asian students at 0.22%. Additionally, around 27.06% of students receive Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of the student body benefits from federal financial aid aimed at supporting those with financial need.
